metadata.title: Systems, Surroundings And Boundaries
metadata.topic: Thermodynamic system definitions for the first foundation lesson

learningPurpose: Prepare the first thermodynamics foundation lesson with source-gated definitions before any property data or process equations are introduced.

definitions.meaning: The selected matter, region or device considered for a thermodynamics analysis.
Everything outside the selected system boundary for the stated analysis.
The real or imagined surface that separates the system from its surroundings.

governingPrinciples: Thermodynamic analysis starts by declaring the system and boundary.
Boundary choice affects what may cross the boundary and what interactions must be tracked.
Definitions require an approved thermodynamics source before student-use approval.
assumptions: No steam, refrigerant, material or property data is provided.
No thermodynamic process equation is approved by this file.
limitations: Does not define property data, state equations, heat-transfer coefficients, cycles or equipment ratings.
No chapter, section or page reference is available until a real source is onboarded.

workedExample.title: Choose a system boundary
workedExample.purpose: Practise declaring what is inside and outside the analysis boundary.
given: A sealed rigid container is used as a classroom example.
The learner must identify the selected system boundary.
steps: Describe the boundary without assigning property data.
workedExample.answer: The answer is complete only when the system, surroundings and boundary are all stated.

normalOperation: Learners define the boundary before interpreting heat, work or mass transfer.
commonMisconceptions: Starting calculations before the system is defined.
Assuming the same boundary works for every question.
Introducing property data without a verified source.

faultConditions.title: Unstated boundary
symptoms: The learner cannot decide whether mass or energy crosses the boundary.
likelyCauses: The system boundary was not declared before analysis.
faultConditions.safeResponse: Return to the definition step and state the selected system and boundary.

safety.warning: Introductory thermodynamics definitions do not authorise equipment operation, pressure testing or thermal-system design.
safety.studentBoundary: Students must use reviewed learning examples and must not infer real equipment limits.
